name: Serialiser
description: API for serialising and deserialising schema-based data structures to and from Luau buffers.

Given a schema definition, the Serialiser API can automatically pack data structures into a compact binary format suitable for network transmission or storage, and unpack them back into usable data structures.
The API will error on any of the functions if the provided schema configuration is invalid, or if the data provided does not conform to the schema.

functions.name: writeInPlace
description: Writes data into a buffer using the provided schema.
To determine the size of the buffer needed, you can use the `Serialiser.measure` function before calling this one.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.description: The buffer to write the data into.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The schema defining the structure of the data.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data to be serialised according to the schema.

parameters.name: bitOffset
parameters.description: The bit offset in the buffer to start writing at.

returns.name: newBitOffset
returns.description: The new bit offset in the buffer after writing the data.

functions.name: write
functions.description: Writes data into a new buffer using the provided schema and returns the buffer.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data to be serialised according to the schema.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The schema defining the structure of the data.

returns.name: buffer
returns.description: The buffer containing the serialised data.

functions.name: read
functions.description: Reads data from a buffer according to the given schema.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.description: The buffer to read the data from.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The schema defining the structure of the data.

parameters.name: bitOffset
parameters.description: The bit offset in the buffer to start reading from.

returns.name: data
returns.description: The data read from the buffer.

functions.name: measure
description: Measures the number of bits and bytes required to serialise the data using the provided schema.
Useful for determining the size of the buffer needed before performing the actual serialisation with `Serialiser.write`.
Changing `bitOffset` can also affect the measurement, as some schema types add padding to align to the nearest byte.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data to be measured.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The schema defining the structure of the data.

parameters.name: bitOffset
parameters.description: The bit offset to start measuring from.

returns.name: bitsNeeded
returns.description: The number of bits needed to serialise the data.

returns.name: bytesNeeded
returns.description: The number of bytes needed to serialise the data.

functions.name: int
description: Creates an integer schema with optional min and max values.
The range between min and max defines the number of bits needed to serialise the integer.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configuration for the integer schema.

functions.name: string
functions.description: Creates a string schema with an optional maximum length.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configuration for the string schema.

functions.name: float
description: Creates a 32-bit floating-point number schema.
Float serialisation uses IEEE 754 format and requires byte-alignment (padding bits are automatically added if necessary).

functions.name: double
description: Creates a 64-bit floating-point number schema.
Double serialisation uses IEEE 754 format and requires byte-alignment (padding bits are automatically added if necessary).

functions.name: quantizedFloat
description: Creates a quantized floating-point number schema.
Quantized floats map a continuous range to discrete integer steps,
providing a space-efficient way to represent floating-point values with controlled precision.
This is useful for network transmission where exact float precision is not required.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configuration for the quantized float schema.

functions.name: vector3
functions.description: Creates a Vector3 schema with configurable component serialisation.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configuration for the Vector3 schema.

functions.name: array
description: Creates an array schema with either a maximum variable length (given by `config.maxLength`) or a fixed length (given by `config.fixedLength`).
You must specify either `maxLength` or `fixedLength`, but not both.
Variable-length arrays require a few more bits to store the length, but allow for any number of elements up to the max.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configuration for the array schema.

functions.name: table
description: Creates an empty table schema.
Use `Serialiser.withField` to add fields to the table.

functions.name: withField
description: Adds a field to a table schema, mutating it in the process.
Fields are serialised and deserialised in the order they are added.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The table schema to add the field to.

parameters.name: fieldName
parameters.description: The name of the field.

parameters.name: fieldSchema
parameters.description: The schema for the field value.

returns.name: schema
returns.description: The table schema that was passed in (for method chaining).

classes.name: IntSchemaConfig
description: Schema configuration for serialising integers up to 32 bits in size.
Integers are encoded as a range to handle both signed and unsigned integers efficiently.
The `min` and `max` properties define the inclusive range of values that can be represented.
The default range can represent any 32-bit signed integer.

properties.name: min
properties.description: The minimum integer value (inclusive) that can be represented.

properties.name: max
properties.description: The maximum integer value (inclusive) that can be represented.

classes.name: StringSchemaConfig
description: Schema configuration for serialising strings.
Strings are encoded as a length prefix followed by individual character bytes (0-255).

properties.name: maxLength
properties.description: The maximum length of the string.

classes.name: QuantizedFloatSchemaConfig
description: Schema configuration for serialising quantized floating-point numbers.
Quantized floats provide a space-efficient way to represent floating-point values
by mapping a continuous range `[min, max]` to a discrete number of integer steps.
The precision and size is determined by the number of steps: more steps = higher precision but more bits required.

properties.name: min
properties.description: The minimum value (inclusive) that can be represented.

properties.name: max
properties.description: The maximum value (inclusive) that can be represented.

properties.name: steps
properties.description: The number of discrete steps to divide the range into.

classes.name: Vector3SchemaConfig
description: Schema configuration for serialising Vector3 values.
By default, each component (x, y, z) is serialised as a 32-bit float.
You can customize this by providing a different `componentSchema` (e.g., quantized floats for reduced bandwidth).

properties.name: componentSchema
properties.description: The schema to use for each component (x, y, z).

classes.name: ArraySchemaConfig
description: Schema configuration for serialising arrays.
Arrays can be either variable-length or fixed-length:
- Variable-length arrays (defined by `maxLength`) store the actual length in the buffer, allowing arrays of different sizes up to `maxLength`.
- Fixed-length arrays (defined by `fixedLength`) do not store length in the buffer, but require the array to always have `fixedLength` elements.
You must provide either `maxLength` or `fixedLength`, but not both.

properties.name: maxLength
properties.description: The maximum number of elements in a variable-length array. Cannot be used with `fixedLength`.

properties.name: fixedLength
properties.description: The exact number of elements in a fixed-length array. Cannot be used with `maxLength`.

properties.name: elementSchema
properties.description: The schema for each element in the array.
